sections.h2: What the Catawba County Register of Deeds records
sections.html:
The office records and keeps deeds, deeds of trust, satisfactions, powers of attorney, plats, easements, rights of way, assumed names and similar land documents. It also holds birth and death records, issues marriage licenses and administers notary oaths. Land records begin in 1842, the year the county was carved out of Lincoln County, which keeps anything older.

The counter is open for recording and for viewing filed records on weekdays from eight in the morning to five in the afternoon, holidays excepted. The phone number is (828) 465-1573. Indexes and images go online once a document is recorded, though they have not been verified. Recorded documents are scanned within one business day.

Voters elect the register. The office may not prepare documents or advise on legal questions, so a deed needs an attorney's drafting. Wills and divorces belong to the clerk of superior court at (828) 695-6100.

A paper filer delivers the signed, acknowledged deed with payment. An electronic filer goes through one of two eRecording companies: Simplifile (800-460-5657) or CSC (866-652-0111). The filer completes a memorandum of understanding with the company before the first submission. For 2023 the county counted 16,868 eRecorded real estate documents, a 74 percent average.

Paper filers should check a short list before the trip:

  • A deed cannot be accepted without the buyer's present mailing address on it.
  • A map or real estate instrument must name and address whoever receives it after recording.
  • Anything you want mailed back requires a stamped, addressed envelope big enough to hold it.
  • The instrument must meet the state's recording standards, and the office uses Times New Roman as its standard font.
  • A cover sheet may be required for some documents, so ask first if you are unsure.

Timing matters because of G.S. 47-18. Until a conveyance is registered where the land lies, it does not protect against lien creditors or later buyers who paid value, and priority runs by registration time. Ask your closing attorney when the deed will reach the register.

Recording fees are set by state statute, and the county adds a few surcharges. The excise tax is separate, and the seller pays it.

Catawba County recording charges
Document or serviceCharge
General instruments, a deed among them$26.00 covers pages 1 to 15; each page beyond adds $4.00
Loan security instruments (mortgage, deed of trust)$64.00 covers pages 1 to 35; each page beyond adds $4.00
Subdivision plat$21.00 for every sheet
Paper that fails the state's format standards$25.00 extra
Assignment citing several deeds of trust$10 each after the first one cited
Instrument naming over 20 parties$2 for every extra party indexed
Photocopy of a recorded deed$.25 a page
Photocopy of a recorded plat$2.00 flat
Conveyance excise tax$1.00 per $500 of value, rounded up by fraction

The county states the tax as $2.00 per $1,000 of price, owed by the seller, and no stamp is due when nothing was paid for the transfer. Satisfactions of deeds of trust record free. Payment can be cash, a business check or a debit or credit card.

Half the excise tax stays in the county general fund and half, net of refunds and an allowance, goes to the state.

sections.h2: Looking up a property by address
sections.html:
The register's records describe land by legal description, not by street address, so an address search belongs with Tax Mapping. Three county numbers cover most seller questions:

  • Register of Deeds, (828) 465-1573, for recording, copies and the index.
  • Tax Mapping, (828) 465-8420, for matching an address to a parcel.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, (828) 695-6100, for wills and divorce records.

Mapping staff or the online real estate maps will do the address lookup. The GIS map is not a legal or binding map. Then take the parcel details to the Register of Deeds online deed search to read the chain of title.

The office cannot correct a missing item, error or misspelling on an original recorded document under G.S. 132-3, so expect to need an attorney for a correction. If a deed is lost, the office can issue a certified copy bearing its seal, which carries the same weight as the original.

The recording of a deed, more than the paper itself, is the main evidence of ownership. A seller who inherited or bought long ago should look for the vesting deed in the index before listing.

sections.h2: How recording ties to selling a house
sections.html:
A financed sale produces up to three recordings: the deed into the buyer, the buyer's deed of trust, and a satisfaction of the seller's old loan, which records without charge. Options, contracts to convey and leases longer than three years need registration too if they are to bind later purchasers.

Chapter 47H governs contract-for-deed sales of one to four family homes in which the seller holds title through five or more payments. The seller must record the contract, or a memorandum of it, within five business days, and the buyer's right to cancel lasts through the third business day. A seller who used that structure should check the index for the memorandum.

Property tax runs alongside recording. The county's tax office, not the register, can state what is owed on the parcel, and any deferred circuit breaker balance comes due on transfer.

The county measures 413 square miles in the Blue Ridge foothills. The 2025 estimate is 170,172 people and 77,827 housing units. The median owned home was worth $241,600 in 2020-2024, and owners live in 72.2 percent of homes.

An old tract's chain of title can run back past 1842, and records before that year are held in Lincoln County.

faqs.q: Where is the Catawba County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Recording hours are 8 to 5 on weekdays, holidays excepted, and the phone is (828) 465-1573. Ask for the office's current street address when you call. eRecording is also available.

faqs.q: What are the charges for filing a deed with Catawba County?
faqs.a: The fee table above lists each charge. Page count drives the base fee, a $25.00 surcharge applies if the format rules are missed, and the seller separately owes the conveyance excise tax. Call (828) 465-1573 to confirm a total before you send a check.

faqs.q: Can Catawba County record a deed electronically?
faqs.a: Yes. The county accepts all document types for eRecording through Simplifile (800-460-5657) and CSC (866-652-0111). The submitter completes a memorandum of understanding with the provider first.

faqs.q: Does the Register of Deeds prepare deeds in Catawba County?
faqs.a: No. State law bars the office from preparing legal documents or giving legal advice, so you need an attorney to draft or correct a deed. The office can show you how to use the indexes and can issue certified copies of recorded deeds at $.25 per page.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax in Catawba County?
faqs.a: The grantor, meaning the seller, settles it with the register before the deed is accepted for recording. The tax runs $1.00 on every $500 of consideration, with part of $500 counted as a full unit. Where nothing was exchanged, no stamp applies.
